title: Which athlete are you under pressure?
dek: Serena, Jordan, Messi, Biles, Ali, Brady or Marta. Twelve questions about the last two minutes and what you do when it's on the line.

questions.prompt: Two minutes left, down by one, and the coach looks at the bench. Your hand is already up.

options.label: Give me the ball
Put me in to set someone else up
Change the play. This one's dead
One sentence to calm them down

questions.prompt: You're in the tunnel before a final. The person next to you is being sick from nerves.

options.label: Hand on the shoulder. Say nothing
Tell them they're about to have the best game of their life
Go through the plan again, quietly
Leave them to it. Focus is private

questions.helper: Not the nicest one. The one you'd compete in.

options.label: An empty track at sunrise
options.alt: Runners on a track at a stadium

options.label: A court with the crowd right on top of it
options.alt: Players on an indoor basketball court

options.label: A pitch, wide open, no shelter
options.alt: A green football pitch under open sky

options.label: A gym at 6am, nobody watching
options.alt: An empty gym with weights and equipment

questions.prompt: I keep a mental list of people who doubted me.
The referee makes a call that is obviously, hilariously wrong.

options.label: Argue until the crowd joins in
Laugh, then play the next phase
Use it. Channel it into the next point
Reset everyone. The call is done

questions.prompt: You should be a good person before a good competitor.
You can have one of these forever:

options.label: A body that never gets injured
A crowd that never doubts you

questions.prompt: A teammate is having the worst night of their career. There's a timeout.

options.label: Tell them the truth, then give them the ball
Carry their share without mentioning it
Make them laugh, then reset
Change what you're asking them to do

questions.prompt: I celebrate other people's wins louder than my own.
A loss you deserved is worth more than a win you didn't.
The final whistle goes. You won.

options.label: Find the teammate who almost quit
Already thinking about the next one
Celebrate like it's the last time
Stand still and take it in

results.name: Serena Williams
results.blurb: When it matters you get louder, not quieter. You want the ball, the serve, the final word, and you're not embarrassed by that. Your intensity has an edge to it and the edge is the point — it's how you turn pressure into a performance.
strengths: Wants the decisive moment
Performs best under the most pressure
Sets the standard for everyone nearby
results.watchOut: Not every opponent is a war. Save the full voltage for when it counts.

results.name: Michael Jordan
results.blurb: You remember who doubted you, who got picked first, and what the score was in a game nobody else recalls. That archive is fuel, and it works. You hold yourself and everyone around you to a standard that is inspiring for about four minutes and exhausting after that.
strengths: Competitive in a way that raises the ceiling
Turns a slight into preparation
Delivers when everyone is watching
results.watchOut: The grudge is a battery that leaks. Some people are just having a bad day.

results.name: Lionel Messi
results.tagline: Makes the difficult thing look obvious
results.blurb: You do the impossible quietly and then act surprised that anyone noticed. Your instinct is always the pass, not the shot — you'd rather set up the moment than be photographed in it. The people who play with you look better than they are, and they know it.
strengths: Sees the option nobody else sees
Makes teammates better
Calm when the tempo rises
results.watchOut: The unselfish option isn't always the right one. Take the shot occasionally.

results.name: Simone Biles
results.tagline: Rewrites the difficulty, then lands it
results.blurb: You're not trying to win the existing contest, you're changing what's possible in it. You practise the terrifying thing until it's boring. You also know the difference between pushing through and damaging yourself, which is a rarer skill than either.
strengths: Expands what counts as achievable
Discipline without theatrics
Knows when to stop — and does
results.watchOut: Not everything needs to be the hardest version. Let something be easy.

results.name: Muhammad Ali
results.tagline: Wins the room before the whistle
results.blurb: You understand that confidence is a performance that becomes real. You talk, you take up space, you make the occasion bigger than it is — and then you back it up. You also know exactly when to be serious, which is why people follow you.
strengths: Turns pressure into theatre
Says the brave thing in public
Stands for something beyond the result
results.watchOut: The performance needs an off switch. Some rooms just want the quiet version.

results.name: Tom Brady
results.blurb: You're not the most spectacular person in the room; you're the one who keeps being right at the end. Preparation, patience, the short correct pass. You treat talent as a floor and habit as the actual advantage, and you'll still be doing this long after everyone else gets bored.
strengths: Consistency over years, not weeks
Reads the situation before it unfolds
Wins ugly without apologising
results.watchOut: The system isn't the whole story. Leave room for the lucky, unplanned thing.

results.name: Marta
results.tagline: Plays like it's still the best day of her life
results.blurb: You haven't let the seriousness of the thing ruin it. You play with joy, you celebrate other people's goals, you laugh when it goes wrong. That's not a lack of ambition — it's the reason you're still doing it when more decorated people have quit.
strengths: Keeps the fun in the work
Lifts a team by enjoying it
Resilient in a way that looks easy
results.watchOut: Joy doesn't replace the hard conversation. Have the difficult one, then play.
